content.text:
**Repaired finding: deviation** (validated, `ok:true`).

What changed and why:

- The substantive elements of the rule remain satisfied — 19.1 (professional/workmanlike + conformity), 19.3 (compliance with law, no malicious code), 19.4 (repair/replace/re-perform plus refund, non-exclusive), 19.5 (disclaimer preserves express warranties).
- The residual gap is **duration**: Deliverables — which under the § 1.4 definition include configurations, integrations and similar software work product — carry only a **ninety-day** conformance period, short of our preferred **12 months for software**. Hosted Services are already warranted for the full subscription term, so no change is needed there.
- Minimal redline: 19.2 "For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later," → "For twelve (12) months after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later,". This reaches the preferred position and states the period in months/numerals, curing the earlier ambiguity from the spelled-out figure.
- Comment offers the fallback (express "ninety (90) days") if Vendor resists, provided the 19.4 remedy stays intact.
